engagement_title: Ferncroft Nursery spring season tag run: eighteen stocked varieties brought to one bench look, two printed tag formats reverse engineered into live merges, and the department bench cards handed back editable
vertical: Automotive, industrial and agriculture, specifically retail horticulture: an heirloom specialty nursery and garden centre in Litchfield County, Connecticut, running a spring season plant list across four planting departments
real_brief_anchor: The ledger carries no single quoted posting for this row, so the anchor is stated honestly as the marketplace archetype it is built from rather than invented as a quotation. The recurring Upwork and Freelancer.com listing of exactly this shape is a garden centre or nursery asking for a variable data tag or label run: a season spreadsheet of varieties plus a folder of variety photographs plus last year's printed tag as the only surviving artwork, with the deliverable named as one print ready file for the tag printer and, very often, separate files per department or per bench. Those posts consistently arrive without a native layout file, with the spreadsheet kept in the growers' own shorthand, and with the request phrased as goals (get the tags printed, keep last year's look, make the prices right) rather than as method. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that the honest fuller commission rather than a data entry exercise: a flat press PDF converts into a live merge template headlessly, one record per page is confirmed, per row photographs genuinely bind through an image column, a rendered page of the converted document can be traced back into vector, and an authored HTML page becomes a native editable Express document for the bench cards the garden centre repaints every season.
client_one_liner: Our spring list is eighteen varieties, the tag printer wants one file by the end of the month, and all we have is last year's printed tags and a spreadsheet the growers keep in their own shorthand.
client_brief:
Ferncroft Nursery, spring season tag run

We are a small heirloom nursery in Litchfield County. We grow perennials, herbs, shrubs and a short specimen list, and we sell from our own benches. Spring opening is the last Saturday of April and every plant on the benches needs its tag by then.

The list. Our season list comes out of the growing office as a spreadsheet. It has the common name, the botanical name, the department, the care line, the pot size and the price. The growers keep it in their own order and their own shorthand and it has never been tidied up for a printer.

The pictures. There is a photograph of every variety, taken on a phone at the benches over the last few weeks. They were not shot as a set and they need to look like one, because the tags hang side by side on a rack and a tag that looks like a different shop is the one a customer distrusts.

The tags. We do not have design files. What we have are the two tags the printer ran last spring: the small hanging tag that goes in the pot, and the larger bench tag we stand next to the specimen shrubs. Both are the right look and we want to keep both.

Our mark is routed and painted into the slate sign at the gate. There is a photograph of it. We would like it back as artwork so it can go on the tags and on anything else.

What we need back. One print file for the tag printer covering everything we are actually stocking this spring, in department order so the benches can be filled straight from it. The tags split out per department, because four different people fill four different benches. And the bench cards we hang over each department, as something we can edit ourselves next season.

We are not a big box nursery. Our plants run eighteen to ninety five dollars and people buy them for provenance, so the tag should read like a plant person wrote it.
price_band_and_audience: An heirloom specialty grower at eighteen to ninety five dollars a plant, buyer thirty five to sixty five, who reads the botanical name and asks where the stock came from. The band is load bearing: at this price the tag is provenance led and botanical forward, the Latin sits with real presence, the care information is set quietly, the price is small and the photograph is a supporting note rather than the headline. The same eighteen varieties at a six dollar big box band would correctly be tagged the other way round, price loud, photograph filling the tag, care icons oversized, common name only, and shipping that treatment here makes a ninety five dollar specimen shrub read as clearance stock. Push the other way into a fine press botanical register with no price and no care line at all and the tag stops doing the job a garden centre tag does. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Grown for the people who ask where it came from.
brand_identity.sector: Retail horticulture: an heirloom specialty nursery and garden centre selling perennials, herbs, shrubs and a short specimen list from its own benches across four planting departments.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A small heirloom grower in Litchfield County, Connecticut, selling from its own benches, with a growing office and four department benches each tended by a different person.
brand_identity.about: Ferncroft Nursery grows heirloom and specialty stock for gardeners who read the botanical name first. Everything is sold off the bench with a tag that reads like a plant person wrote it. Spring opening is the last Saturday of April, and every plant on the rack needs its tag by then.
brand_identity.audience: Gardeners aged thirty five to sixty five who buy for provenance, read the Latin name, and ask where the stock was grown. They distrust a rack where one tag looks like a different shop.
brand_identity.price_positioning: An heirloom specialty grower at eighteen to ninety five dollars a plant, above the six dollar big-box rack and below a fine-press botanical print. The tag is provenance-led and botanical-forward: the Latin carries, the price sits small, the photograph is a supporting note.
brand_identity.typography: A humanist serif with real presence for the common and botanical names, the Latin set in italic beneath, paired with a quiet, small sans for the care line, pot size and price. Restraint is the point: the price should never shout.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, knowledgeable, unhurried, the voice of a grower. Example line the brand would write: 'Slow to establish, then generous for decades. Give it morning sun and patience.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There are no design files. The two tags the printer ran last spring survive only as press PDFs, and the nursery mark exists only routed and painted into the slate sign at the gate, captured in one handheld photograph. The mark and the printed care icons have to be recovered before they can go anywhere new.
brand_identity.values: Provenance and honesty on the bench: the name on the tag is the right name, and the whole rack reads as one careful hand. Restraint signals quality here.

assets_supplied.name: ferncroft_season_list.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Season list exported from the growing office: common name, botanical name, department, care line, pot size, price and a photo column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our season list. The growers keep it the way they like it. Everything we are stocking should be in there."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Twenty one rows for eighteen stocked varieties, because three plants cut from the season after the list was written are still in it and nothing in the row says so except a pot size that never got filled in. It is sorted in bench walking order rather than by department, the merge honours row order and a finished file gives no sign that its order is wrong, and the photo column is a plain header holding bare filenames, which is not the shape a variable image binding accepts.

assets_supplied.name: ferncroft_hangtag_2025_PRINTER.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press PDF the printer ran for last spring's small hanging tag, at its proper trim, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The tag that goes in the pot. It is the right look, keep it." Prints the common name, the botanical name in italic underneath, the care line, the pot size, the price and a variety photograph, plus a row of small care icons along the foot.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed face reads as six separately labelled fields but the placed photograph splits the flow into only two text frames, so most of those lines share one continuous story and can only be driven by ordered offset arithmetic inside it. The readout of that story silently omits the run holding the italic botanical name while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed and every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length.

assets_supplied.name: ferncroft_benchtag_2025_PRINTER.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press PDF for the larger bench tag that stands beside the specimen shrubs, same house look, same faces, at a much larger trim.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The big one we stand next to the specimens. Same look, bigger. We want both formats."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What prints as a photograph panel on this format was a flat tinted panel in the original artwork rather than a placed image, so nothing about the printed tag distinguishes it from the hanging tag's real photo frame.

assets_supplied.name: ferncroft_variety_photos/ (18 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Phone photographs of each variety taken at the growing benches across several weeks, at whatever distance the grower happened to be standing.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One picture of every variety. Different days, different weather, but they are all there."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: They were shot across weeks of changing light and at wildly different distances, so several frames are already tight and small and cannot reach the tag's photo frame placement geometry at native scale, while the crop tool will interpolate up to a hard cap and report having done so only inside its own tradeoff record. Two of the eighteen turn out to be the same plant photographed at two stages, and one stocked variety has no photograph at all, which no filename reveals.

assets_supplied.name: ferncroft_slate_sign.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the painted slate sign at the nursery gate, the mark routed into the slate and filled with a pale paint.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our mark. It only exists on the gate now."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark is paint sitting inside a routed groove, so its own edge carries a cast shadow line all the way round, and a prompt naming the sign returns the slate rather than the paint.

acceptance_bar: One print file contains every variety we are actually stocking this spring and nothing we are not, page count equal to stocked row count exactly, in department order rather than in the order the growers keep the list.

Every field on every tag is that variety's own: the botanical name, the care line, the pot size and the price all change from tag to tag wherever the list says they change. A field that is identical on every tag because it never became variable fails the run.
Every tag that can carry a photograph carries that variety's own photograph, and no picture stands in for two varieties.
The department subsets are complete and disjoint: every stocked variety appears in exactly one, and each subset holds exactly the department it names.

No delivered image exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop's returned tradeoff record carries an upscale entry. A tag photograph brought to size by enlargement fails even where it looks acceptable on screen.

The eighteen photographs read as one rack when the tags hang side by side: one white point, one crop logic, one distance from the plant. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named, not shipped at eighty percent.
The second format is delivered honestly for what its own artwork can carry, with the limitation named plainly rather than papered over with a picture that is not really there.

The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, and still reading as our mark at the size it prints on the small tag.
The care icons come back as artwork rather than as a screenshot, recovered from what we already print rather than redrawn into something that is not our icon.
The department bench cards are one editable document with live text we can retype, a real table for the season list, and the mark as real vector shapes.
One type system across the bench cards, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer and the actual weight used.
The note states what changed in our list and why, what was applied per photograph, every resize any tool reported, and anything the printer asks for that these files cannot carry.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout, merge template authoring and print render
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (mapping and validation modes), prepare_indd_merge_template (params.mappingJson as a JSON string), document_merge_data_layout (outputSpecs, recordRange, additionalImageFiles), document_render_layout (resolution, pageRange, createSeparateFiles)
adobe_surfaces.role: The print half of the commission on both formats. Each printer PDF is converted, its real frame inventory read from the round tripped IDML, a merge template authored against whatever that document actually exposes, then the season run delivered as one ordered press file plus per department subsets. The render stage also produces the high resolution page raster that the icon recovery is traced from, which is the only honest way to get the client's own icons back.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs and upscale_factor), image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Bringing eighteen phone frames shot across weeks of weather to one rack look, cutting each to the tag's photo frame geometry without enlargement, recovering the nursery mark at ink level off a photographed painted slate, and tracing the existing care icons off a high resolution render of the client's own printed tag rather than inventing replacements.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The department bench cards and the season price sheet as one native editable document at two canvas sizes, which is the only surface here that composes free form fixed canvas layout. The price sheet is a genuine table, the recovered mark and the recovered icons go in as inline SVG so they stay vector, every photograph is carried as embedded image data, and family and weight are declared on every text element.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the bench cards and the handover, judged against an eighteen to ninety five dollar heirloom band and a provenance reading buyer. The recommender refuses to pair by design so the pairing is the agent's own art direction, numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be read off a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the nursery does not have, a potting bench and hand tools band for the bench card headers, IP clean and at genuine camera scale with generative tech candidates excluded. The Boards half persists the shared selects set the owner signs off from, placed within the twelve per call cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The tags are a variable data run at one record per page, which is a merge job; the bench cards are free form fixed canvas layout, which only the authoring surface does. The brief pins both, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role, because the run depends on knowing which URL is which variety.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Read the season list against the photo folder and against what the client says they are stocking: row count, rows with a missing pot size, the order actually present, header hygiene, the shape of the photo column, and which photographs correspond to which variety.
trajectory.judgement: The growers' list and the stocked list are not the same list and neither is authoritative on its own. Bench order and department order are both plausible orders and only one of them fills a bench.
trajectory.produces: A reconciled, department ordered data file for the stocked list, an image column in the shape the binding actually accepts, and a written list of every change made to the client's export.

trajectory.action: Preview all eighteen frames and triage them: which week and which weather each belongs to, which are off level, how far the grower was standing, how much of the frame the plant occupies, and which frames are already tight.
trajectory.judgement: Eighteen usable snapshots and one rack are different things. Shooting distance is the variable nobody names and it governs both the crop and whether the crop is reachable at all.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering illuminant, tilt, subject occupancy and native frame size.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one bench target off the best lit frame and bring each of the eighteen to it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The destination is a rack, not eighteen nice pictures of plants. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong across weeks of changing weather; foliage green is also the hue that goes wrong first under a global warmth move.
trajectory.produces: Eighteen graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Apply confined corrections where a whole frame move goes wrong, selecting by the material's own visual properties rather than by the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the pot pulls the selection to the terracotta. Frames shot against wet bench timber need the foliage held while the ground moves.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a whole frame move would have taken the foliage yellow or the bench muddy.

trajectory.action: Cut each frame to the hanging tag's photo frame geometry with one crop logic across the set, reading the returned tradeoff record for any upscale entry before accepting the crop.
trajectory.judgement: One crop logic across eighteen means the plant sits at one distance on every tag, which is what makes a rack read as a rack. Placement geometry comes from the printed tag and the converted document, not from what looks nice full frame.
trajectory.produces: Eighteen tag photographs at one crop logic with their tradeoff records.

trajectory.action: Recover the nursery mark off the slate sign: an ink level selection naming the paint's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the sign takes the slate. The routed groove puts a shadow line around the mark's own edge, so what the selection takes and what the trace makes of it are two separate judgements.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark plus a colour accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Convert both printer PDFs to live documents, round trip each through IDML, and read what each one actually is: frame counts, real bounds, applied faces and sizes, object styles and existing links.
trajectory.judgement: Two tags that print as the same design in two sizes are not necessarily the same document, and what a printed face looks like says nothing about what the conversion exposes as addressable frames. Promising a field to a frame before looking is how a run ships half mapped.
trajectory.produces: Two written frame inventories, and a decision about which fields can live where on each format.

trajectory.action: Render a page of the converted hanging tag at high resolution, then recover the care icon row off that render at ink level and trace it into vector.
trajectory.judgement: The icons already exist in the client's own printed artwork, so recovering them is archaeology rather than invention, and rendering the converted document is the only route that produces a raster clean enough to trace.
trajectory.produces: The client's own care icon set as placeable vector artwork.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct each frame's true story text from the IDML content runs, compute every offset from that string, build the mapping with text mappings for the tag's lines plus an image mapping for the photo frame, run it back through validation, prepare the merge template, then re-export IDML and confirm every expected placeholder is actually present.
trajectory.judgement: A validator that says valid and a preparation step that says success are both reports about the request, not about the document. The only evidence a placeholder exists is finding it in the round tripped story.
trajectory.produces: A live merge template whose placeholders are confirmed present by inspection rather than by tool response.

trajectory.action: Merge the reconciled stocked list to one press file in department order, binding each variety's own photograph, and read a sample of the merged tags against the list line by line.
trajectory.judgement: A file with the right number of pages and the right names on them can still be wrong in every other field. The list is what the tag has to agree with, variety by variety.
trajectory.produces: One press file for the whole stocked season plus a line by line reading of sample records.

trajectory.action: Produce the per department subsets by record range off the same template and data, and check each subset for completeness and disjointness against the reconciled list.
trajectory.judgement: Subsetting only works because the data was put in department order first; on the growers' original order the ranges would be meaningless while still producing files that look correct.
trajectory.produces: Four department subsets, each verified complete and disjoint.

trajectory.action: Produce the sign off proofs at genuine print resolution at trim by rendering the merged document rather than by asking the merge for a raster.
trajectory.judgement: Print resolution is a property of the render stage; a page sized raster carrying a print name is the thing that gets signed off and then fails at the printer.
trajectory.produces: Proof rasters at real resolution at trim, with their dimensions recorded.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the potting bench band, filter to photography, exclude generative tech results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the bench target rather than the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame graded into the same world.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against an heirloom band and a provenance reading buyer: the botanical name has to carry, which is a type decision and not a size decision. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the department bench cards and the season price sheet at their own canvas sizes, with the price sheet as a real table, the mark and the recovered icons as inline SVG inside explicitly sized top left anchored wrappers, every photograph carried as embedded image data, family and weight declared on every text element, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: An auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how quietly the price sits and how much presence the Latin gets.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the bench card set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.surface: Adobe Express, then Boards and handover
trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, verify through both available channels (resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the rest), then create the selects board, add the graded set and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, and write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. A partial board response is partial, and the vector mark is not boardable so it belongs in the note.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an audited export, a persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

trajectory.action: Write the reconciliation and limitation record: list changes, per frame parameters, every resize any tool reported, the proof resolutions, what each tag format can and cannot carry, and anything the printer asks for that these files cannot supply.
trajectory.judgement: A thing the supplied artwork physically cannot do has to be said plainly and early, because the tag printer will otherwise find it in the last week of April.
trajectory.produces: The handover note the owner and the tag printer both work from.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether these particular phone frames can reach the tag's photo frame geometry at one crop logic without being enlarged. The frames were taken at whatever distance the grower happened to be standing, so occupancy varies wildly, and the ones where the grower stood close are already tight. A crop to the tag's geometry on those returns a clean, correctly sized, entirely plausible looking picture while having interpolated up to a hard cap, and it says so nowhere in its message, its warnings or its errors: the only trace is an entry inside the returned tradeoff record. Which of the eighteen this happens to is a property of each file and is not visible by looking at the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the tag's placement geometry is only known once the printer's document has been converted and read, and there is no parameter that forbids the enlargement. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the pictures were taken at the benches on a phone over several weeks, which is the client describing their photographs rather than a disclosure about resolution. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a per frame decision about a different crop logic for the set, not the same crop again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read the tradeoff record on every crop, then re-plan the crop logic for the whole set around what the tightest usable frame can actually give at native scale, re-cut all eighteen to that logic so the rack still reads as one rack, and name any frame that cannot be brought to it rather than shipping it enlarged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A rack of tags where several varieties are represented by soft interpolated pictures at ninety five dollars a plant, and a set that no longer reads as one set because the affected frames were the only ones cropped differently.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the second tag format actually is as an editable document. Both printed tags carry what reads as a variety photograph in the same house layout at two sizes, and nothing about the printed artwork, the file, or the client's description separates them. The conversion is where they diverge: what looks like a photograph panel on the larger format was never a placed image, so that document comes across as a continuous text flow with no graphic frame anywhere in it, and there is nowhere for a per variety photograph to bind at all. The mapping strategies the two formats need are therefore different in kind, not in degree, and the difference exists only inside the converted structure.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no care in the mapping prevents it; frame granularity out of a PDF is not under the agent's control, and an agent that promised the same treatment on both formats would have been reading the same evidence the client was. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the two tags are the same look at two sizes and asks for both, which is true of what prints. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the second format needs a structurally different plan, and the photograph it cannot carry has to be dealt with somewhere else entirely.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the specimen format around what its own document can carry, drive its lines by ordered offset arithmetic inside the single story it exposes, decide honestly whether the specimen varieties get a photograph on a different surface instead, and rewrite the department subsets so the specimen department is not silently promised something the format cannot do.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A specimen bench of ninety five dollar shrubs tagged with an empty tinted panel where the customer expects to see the plant, discovered by the owner on opening Saturday.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the mapping built against the hanging tag actually landed on every field. The tag's printed face reads as six labelled fields, the readout of its story looks well formed, the validator returns valid with no warnings and the placeholder step reports completing successfully. The readout silently omits one run while keeping its line break, so every offset computed past it is short by exactly that run's length and two of the mappings never become placeholders at all. The merged tags then carry the template's own static text in those positions, and because that static text is a perfectly ordinary care line and a plausible price, a merged tag read on its own looks completely correct. Only reading tag against tag against the season list, variety by variety, shows that those two fields never change.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and there is no parameter that makes the readout complete; an agent that computed its offsets from the readout the tool handed it would have followed the documented chain exactly. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the growers' list has never been tidied, which is about the data, not about the template's story. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix is to reconstruct the true story text from the round tripped document and recompute every offset against that string, which is a different source of truth rather than the same computation again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the offsets from the reconstructed story, rebuild the mapping, prepare the template again, confirm every expected placeholder by inspecting the round tripped document rather than by reading the response, then re-merge the whole run and re-read sample tags against the list before any subset is cut.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eighteen tags printed with the same care line and the same price on every one of them, which on a nursery bench means a shrub priced like a herb and a shade plant sold to somebody who will put it in full sun.

deliverables.name: Ferncroft spring tag press run and department subsets
deliverables.spec: One press file for the tag printer covering every stocked variety and nothing cut from the season, one record per page, page count equal to stocked row count and page order equal to department order, every field variable where the season list says it varies and every tag carrying its own variety photograph. Plus four department subsets, complete and disjoint, cut off the same template and data.

deliverables.name: Ferncroft variety photography brought to one rack
deliverables.spec: Eighteen phone frames shot across weeks of changing weather brought to one bench target (one white point, one crop logic, one distance from the plant), foliage held true rather than dragged along by the ground correction, plus one licensed camera scale potting bench frame graded into the same world. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with the returned tradeoff record for each, and a per frame parameter log.

deliverables.name: Recovered Ferncroft mark and the recovered care icon set
deliverables.spec: The nursery mark recovered from a photograph of a painted routed slate sign as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, delivered as a single colour mark and a colour accurate variant. Paired with the client's own care icons recovered by tracing a high resolution render of their own printed tag rather than redrawn, so the icons on the new tags are the icons the customers already know.

deliverables.name: Department bench cards and season price sheet as one editable document plus its source

decision_gates: Which deliverables are a variable data run at one record per page and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout.
Which list governs, the growers' export or the stocked season, and how to change the export without changing the horticultural copy that has to stay as written.
What order the run prints in, when the list arrives in one plausible order and the benches need another.
How far to push the wettest and the brightest frames toward one bench target before they stop being worth saving, versus naming them.
Whether a correction is a whole frame move or a confined one, given that foliage green is the hue a global warmth move takes first.
What one crop logic across eighteen frames actually is, once shooting distance turns out to be the variable nobody named.

Selection wording on the slate sign: naming the sign takes the substrate, naming the paint's own visual properties takes the mark, and the routed groove's shadow line has to be judged separately from either.
Whether the care icons are recovered from what the nursery already prints or replaced with something new, and what that choice costs a customer who already reads the old ones.
Which fields can be addressed as frames and which have to be driven by ordered arithmetic inside one story, decided per format rather than once.
Where print resolution actually comes from in this chain, since the stage that produces the raster and the stage that controls its resolution are not the same stage.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged on whether the botanical name carries at an heirloom band, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How quietly the price sits. At this band restraint is the design, and a loud, price led tag is a correct looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pretty pictures of plant tags. IDENTITY: these are this nursery's own eighteen varieties with their own botanical names, care lines and prices, their own mark recovered off the gate sign rather than reinvented, and their own care icons recovered off the tag their customers already read; a regenerated mark is a different nursery's mark and a regenerated icon means nothing to anybody. SPEC: the tag printer needs one file at trim whose page count equals the stocked row count in department order, plus four complete and disjoint subsets and proofs at a stated resolution, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for, and a tag whose Latin name is hallucinated is a plant sold under the wrong name. EDITABILITY: the bench cards are defined by being edited by the nursery next season. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: can this phone frame reach the tag's geometry without being enlarged, does this second format have anywhere to put a photograph at all, does this field actually change from tag to tag.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt in both mapping and validator modes, prepare_indd_merge_template and document_merge_data_layout are verified fully headless and synchronous, and a flat press PDF was reverse engineered end to end into a live merge template whose placeholders were confirmed by unzipping the round tripped IDML. One record per page is confirmed for PDF output, record range subsetting is verified for single records and ranges, and per row image binding through an image column plus per file image inputs is verified visually, so eighteen distinct variety photographs genuinely bind. Checkpoint two rests on the documented finding that frame granularity out of a PDF is not under the agent's control and that a continuous flow with no placed images converts to a single text frame with zero graphic frames. Checkpoint three rests on the documented headline trap: the mapping readout dropped a seventeen character run while keeping its line break, the validator still returned valid with zero warnings, the preparation step still reported success and only three of five mappings landed, with all six landing once offsets were recomputed from the true story. Real print resolution is verified through document_render_layout (300 at Letter returned 2550x3300 with matching density) while the merge stage's own resolution parameter is documented as silently ignored, which is why the proof is a separate render and why the icon recovery traces a rendered page rather than a screen grab. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with a returned box, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and upscale factor, fill_area, remove_background and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls; checkpoint one rests on the documented two times interpolation cap reported only inside the tradeoffs array. Ink level recovery off a photographed painted surface, the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero are all live findings. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, a real table survives as a live table with per cell backgrounds and strokes, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset search, and the rendition preview is documented as first artboard only.
